title: Check yourself: The prompt as a specification

questions.stem: A team keeps editing a prompt and judging each edit by reading one reply. Over a month quality seems to drift and nobody can say which edit caused it. What is the best remedy?

options.text: Revert to the version in place when quality last seemed good, and stop editing
options.says: Ruled out because "Without the first two, you cannot tell whether an edit helped", so nobody can know which version was the good one.

options.text: Write the criteria down and score every version on a fixed set of inputs
options.says: Success criteria and test inputs are the preconditions the overview names, and without them no edit can be compared (the success criteria section).

options.text: Have the model rank the edits and keep the one it prefers
options.says: Ruled out because the preconditions include "some ways to empirically test against those criteria", and a model's preference is not one.

options.text: Write the criteria down, then judge each edit by reading one fresh reply
options.says: Ruled out because "Changing a prompt and re-reading one answer is anecdote", so the criteria need a fixed set of inputs to be scored on.

questions.stem: A request asks Claude to read a fifty-page report, judge whether a supplier is at risk and draft a board email. The email's claims are sometimes unsupported. Which restructuring helps most?

options.text: Resend the same request three times and merge the three emails
options.says: Ruled out because the benefit of stages is that "a failure shows up at the stage where it happened", which repetition does not give.

options.text: Request the email first and the assessment afterwards, to compare them
options.says: Ruled out because the stages start with "extract the relevant facts or quotes from the material", so the email cannot come first.

options.text: Add a closing line: "Be careful; do not include unsupported claims"
options.says: Ruled out because "A giant do-everything prompt makes failures hard to locate", and a closing line is a request, not a stage.

options.text: Run stages: pull exact quotes, assess from only those, then write
options.says: Staging with an evidence step first is the pattern the page models on the documentation's quote-first technique, with a code check possible between stages.
